title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting leg still executes the unguarded update_reference_call_status — the guarded mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person SQL is orphaned and the race pin is vacuous
evidence:
form_handler.gleam 1249-1261: `case sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)` — the executed transition. update_reference_call_status.sql:22-24: `WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status` — NO taken_over_at guard, and take-over keeps status contact_initiated (A7 stickiness), so a take-over landing between the token read (row.taken_over_at != "" check, form_handler.gleam:1238) and this UPDATE still matches and yanks a landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction. mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql:16 has `AND taken_over_at IS NULL`, but grep of server/src shows ZERO callers — the module is dead code (only the test calls it). The pin wrong_person_awaiting_sql_has_taken_over_backstop_test (reference_checks_actions_integration_test.gleam:1746,1758) calls `rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)` DIRECTLY while the handler executes a different, unguarded UPDATE — neutralizing the backstop cannot turn it red.
detail: The r3 TOCTOU blocker is not closed: the executed wrong-person path has no taken_over_at backstop, the dedicated guarded SQL ships orphaned, and the race test pins the dead query instead of the handler path.
recommended_fix: Replace the sql.update_reference_call_status call in apply_wrong_person with sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person; rewrite the race test to drive the POST /reference/<token>/wrong-person route with a take-over between read and update.
